headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Great Expectations can expose validation artifacts while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress and no documented verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, agent_a writes validation results and documentation to files, and agent_b has no stated isolation or provenance controls. If outputs are manually copied or file-shared, injected instructions could be misread, but the pathway is not default.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into agent_b prompts or files
IF a shared workspace or clipboard is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep outputs in separate directories
Disable copy-paste between agents during review
Add a provenance header to every transferred artifact
Use read-only exports for agent_a outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches validation results and documentation and can read/write files, while agent_b has allowlisted network egress. Even without explicit shared storage, any shared workspace or transferred artifact could leak sensitive validation content through agent_b's outbound requests. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a validation results are placed in a workspace readable by agent_b
IF agent_b sends prompt or file contents through its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Store agent_a outputs in a separate folder
Redact sensitive fields before transfer
Block agent_b from reading validation-result files
Review allowlisted destinations before any run
Use local-only test data for shared workflows

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can install packages and write files, while agent_b only shows allowlisted egress and no write surface. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so a direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. If both are later pointed at the same directory or repo, conflicts could appear, but that is not default.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same filesystem path
IF agent_b is given write access not shown in its profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent package installs in shared environments
Freeze one agent while the other writes
Use lockfiles for any shared repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces validation results that agent_b could treat as authoritative if chained, and agent_b has no documented verification step or concurrency model. That creates a plausible default pathway for unverified outputs to cascade into downstream actions or reports. Because the handoff is inferred rather than directly documented, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a validation results as facts
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require a verification step before reuse
Mark agent_a outputs as provisional
Have agent_b cite source files explicitly
Add a human review gate for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_a handles documentation and validation results, while agent_b has no declared data classes or compliance constraints. With only docs-only evidence, compliance risk is limited to unknowns rather than a demonstrated breach, so low is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_a or agent_b workflows
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before deployment
Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings for shared artifacts
Review vendor residency requirements
